 Rep.-Elect Donna Miller elected co-president of 120th Congress’s freshman class
 By Provided News 
 November 20, 2026 
 13 
 2 min. 
 Rep.-Elect Donna Miller, center, joins her two co-presidents after freshman class members vote for them to represent the largest class in nearly 100 years in the 120th Congress. Serving with Miller are Rep.-Elect Fred Wellman (MI-02) and Rep.-Elect Dan Koh (MA-06). (Photo Provided) INFORMATION PROVIDED BY REP. ELECT DONNA MILLER’S OFFICE.
 WASHINGTON, D.C. — Rep. Dan Koh (MA-06), Donna Miller (IL-02), and Fred Wellman (MI-02) have been elected co-presidents of the 120th Congress’s freshman class. The Members-elect were chosen by their peers to represent the class before the caucus, leverage its unprecedented size for influence, and promote unity within its members. They will lead the largest freshman class in the House of Representatives in 100 years, with 75 members. “It’s time we deliver for Americans across the country,” said Miller. “That means working together to lower the cost of groceries, gas, healthcare, rent, and mortgages, and to restore faith and trust to our democracy. This freshman class brings fresh ideas and new perspectives, and we have an opportunity to build a stronger path forward. I’m ready to bring this class together, fight for our priorities, and deliver real results for the people we represent.”
 Rep-Elect Donna Miller makes her pitch to freshman class members to serve as co-president of the 120th Congress. Three co-presidents will lead the largest class of new members in nearly 100 years. Also, elected were Rep. Elect Fred Wellman (MI-02) and Rep.-Elect Dan Koh (MA-06). (Photo Provided) “Voters across the country sent Democrats to Congress to stop this president’s grift and deliver a government that works for people. Our mandate is clear: restore accountability and lower costs. We have to prove that voters were right to place their trust in Democrats across the country and that we are ready to fight this President and his destructive agenda on Day One. As co-presidents, we’ll unite this class to fight for those priorities and deliver results. Massachusetts’ Sixth sent me to Washington to fight for them, and we’re not wasting a single day,” said Koh. “After 34 years of Republican representation, Michigan’s 2nd District was ready for change, and voters trusted me to deliver it. It’s time we unite together. This is a moment for bringing our class together and focusing on what unites us. Our constituents are worried about the cost of living, government accountability, and the divisiveness coming out of Washington. As co-presidents, our job is to unite this class around the priorities of the people we represent and get things done,” said Wellman. The co-presidents will work together to create the strongest version of its historically diverse class.
